newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CLF buys five percent of BIL.
newsitem.headline: CLF buys five percent of BIL.

text.p: French bank Credit Local de France has acquired a five percent stake in Banque Internationale a Luxembourg, the Luxembourg bank controlled by CLF's Belgian partner bank Dexia CC, BIL shareholders were told at their annual meeting on Tuesday.
BIL Chairman Gaston Thorn said CLF acquired its stake in an off-market operation, but declined to name the seller.
But a source close to the company told Reuters that the seller was Swiss Geneva-based PSA International, whose cief executive Marc Dumont was a BIL board member until April 1996.
BIL chief executive officer Andre Roelants repeated that BIL's role was to be the private bank and fund management centre of the new Belgian-French Dexia financial group.
BIL is 52-percent onwed by Dexia CC, the Belgian arm of the Dexia group.
A CLF spokesman in Paris confirmed that CLF has had the five percent stake in BIL since late 1996.
The BIL assembly elected CLF Chairman Pierre Richard to its board in place of Belgian businessman Gerald Frere, who had resigned his position, the bank said.
